name: Windows Recovery Partition Editor
description: Windows Recovery Partition Editor resizes the local Windows Recovery Partition to 984MB and injects CAB files to enable optional features and language support. It deploys via a PowerShell script, placing architecture-specific CABs under tools\amd64 or tools\arm64cpu and matching language packs, with an optional backup of OEM images. Detection uses the registry key HKLM:\SOFTWARE\YourCompanyNameHere\Client-Recovery with value 1.0.0.
keywords: how to resize windows recovery partition
author: Niklas Rast

securityCheck.aiSummary: The Windows Recovery Partition Editor is a legitimate admin tool to manage WinRE and related partitions. It does not exhibit obfuscated code, remote downloads, credential theft, data exfiltration, or known malware patterns. However, it performs high-privilege destructive partition operations and Reagentc reconfiguration, which could be risky if misused or tampered with. Recommendations: ensure code is signed, restrict execution to trusted admins, add robust error handling and rollback, log all actions, and provide an explicit rollback path. Also consider safeguarding storage of configuration data in the registry and validating inputs before destructive actions.
